newsitem.title: JAPAN: INSIGHT - Japan Sept SQ not seen denting market much. [CORRECTED 9:55 gmt]
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Japan Sept SQ not seen denting market much. [CORRECTED 9:55 gmt]

text.p: The settlement of Japan's September futures and stock options, or special quotations (SQ), on Friday is not likely to dent the stock market much, although there may be more long than short positions in the market, brokers said on Thursday.

"Net selling positions for each cash stock issue in the Nikkei 225 will probably be about one million to 1.3 million (corrects from "100,000 to 130,000") tomorrow, not much different from past SQs," Nomura Securities Investment Trust Co trader Kazuhiko Maruyama said.
"Rollovers started early this time, so the September net selling (corrects from "open interest") will be only about 200,000 units," he added.
The SQ will be calculated at the opening on Friday.
Yamaichi Securities said it expected net selling positions, including TOPIX issues, to be about 800 million shares, against buying positions of about 500 million shares.
"Although position adjustments are expected to continue throughout the day today, cash stocks are likely to be bruised slightly by the settlement tomorrow," a trader at a second-tier brokerage said.
"But the downside should be limited, and the Nikkei average should shed only 180 to 200 points from the Thursday close," he added.
Public funds, as well as foreign investors buying on dips, were likely to prevent the Nikkei average from plunging, market sources said.
But they said the market was keeping a vigilant watch on Wall Street to see how it reacts to the August producer price index which will be released later today.
They said movements in New York could influence Nikkei futures tomorrow morning, which may prompt investors to build up arbitrage-linked positions, providing the Nikkei with additional support.
